---
title: "Week 6 · Simple and multiple regression. Bias. Linearity"
subtitle: "Recap of the t-test, then the regression line, OLS, multiple regression, bias and efficiency, the six assumptions and linearity"
---

The longest deck of the programme. It opens with an exam-style t-test
assignment, then introduces simple linear regression on farmland prices, extends
it to multiple regression, and discusses what the estimates mean, when they are
biased and efficient, and which assumptions guarantee that. The first
assumption, linearity, is worked through in detail. A self-study section on the
origins of regression closes the deck.

## What the deck covers

-   **Example of an exam assignment** (the t-test recap): a definition
    question, problem introduction, descriptive analysis, checks and balances,
    the effect of technology and of variety on rice yields, how to measure the
    effect of nitrogen fertiliser, and a framework for interpreting any
    statistical test.
-   **(Very) simple linear regression**: regression on population and sample;
    plot size and farmland prices; the regression line; coefficients and their
    interpretation; the OLS algorithm; the population regression function and
    random sampling; sample variation; inference; goodness of fit; key
    takeaways and self-study examples, including CFC-11 in the stratosphere.
-   **Multiple regression**: vocabulary, motivation and interpretation; examples
    (the wage equation, test scores and spending, CEO salary); mechanics; a full
    example on the effect of fuel taxes on petrol consumption, from problem
    formulation and exploratory analysis to estimating simple and multiple
    regressions and interpreting each coefficient.
-   **Bias and efficiency**: sampling from the population; unbiased and
    efficient, unbiased but inefficient, biased but efficient, biased and
    inefficient estimates.
-   **Assumptions of the MLR**: the six assumptions and what each group of
    them guarantees (unbiased; BLUE; classical linear model).
-   **Assumption 1, linearity**: can we draw a straight line through the dots;
    detection with residual plots; resolutions; common linear transformations;
    the Anscombe quartet.
-   Key concepts checklist and a self-study section on the cradle of regression
    analysis: Galton, Yule and the dark past of statistics.

## Data used

-   📊 [CFC-11 daily means at Mauna Loa](../data.qmd#cfc11)
    (`CATS_mlo_F11_Day.dat`), for the self-study ozone example.
-   `fuel2001` (US fuel consumption by state) from the alr4 R package.
-   `gomez.splitsplit` (rice yields by technology and variety) from the agridat
    R package, in the t-test recap.
-   A simulated population of farmland plots, generated by
    [`01-simple-reg-plots.R`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/blob/main/materials/01-simple-reg-plots.R).
